1.

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the appellant/claimant for enhancement against the award dated 06.11.2015 passed by learned 5 th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Durg District - Durg (C.G.), in Claim Case No. 13/2015 whereby compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum, in favour of the appellant has been awarded.

sentences.text: 2. The averment in the claim petition, in brief, is that on 17/09/2010, the applicant was traveling from Tumsar to Bagbahara, Mahasamund in a Santro car bearing registration number C.G. 04 H/9017.
At around 2:30 AM, near Kumhari Desi Bhatti, the driver (Respondent No. 1) of the Santro car C.G. 04 H/9017, while driving at high speed and carelessly, collided with a divider.

As a result,
the applicant sustained injuries to his left arm, and the bone from the shoulder to the arm was fractured and displaced onto the shoulder.
Following the incident, the applicant was admitted to Chandulal Chandrakar Hospital, where he remained for three hours.
He was later admitted in a hospital at Raipur, where surgery was performed on his left arm, extending to the shoulder, and a rod was inserted.
The applicant underwent another surgery later, and the treatment is still ongoing.
Due to the said accident, a case bearing No. 16/2011 under Sections 279, 337, and 338 of the IPC was registered against Respondent No. 1.
The accident occurred due to the high speed and careless driving of the Santro car by Respondent No. 1, who collided with the divider.
Therefore, Respondent No. 2 and Respondent No. 3, the insurance company, are liable to pay compensation.
In this accident, the applicant's left arm was fractured, resulting in permanent disability.
Due to the accident, the applicant has been unable to do any work and has had to employ two people to run his grocery store.
The applicant was 29 years old at the time of the accident.

Due to the permanent disability caused by the accident, as well as the expenses incurred for treatment, the applicant has claimed a total of 21,96,000 (twenty-one lakh ninety-six thousand) from the respondents, along with 12% annual interest as compensation amount 3.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has erred to hold that the disability certificate Exhibit P-1 was issued by Dr. P.C. Deshmukh (PW-1) to the extent of 12%, but the Tribunal has not held the disability of the appellant, which is not appropriate.
He further submits that the applicant was admitted in a hospital at Raipur for about 15 days, where surgery was performed on his left arm, extending to the shoulder, and a rod was inserted.
The applicant underwent another surgery later, and the treatment is still ongoing.
The loss for physical injury suffered by the applicant only Rs.25,000/- has been assessed by the Tribunal.
Furthermore, no amount has been awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of income during treatment and future treatment.
Hence, it is prayed that this appeal may be allowed and needs to be enhanced suitably.

4. No one appeared on behalf of Respondents No.1 & 2.
5.
Learned counsel for Respondents No. 3 opposes the argument advanced by the counsel for the appellant and supported the impugned award.

6. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Gangadhar Agrawal vs Tribhuwan Nayak on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163773540/
2
7. In a motor accident claim case, what is important is that, the compensation to be awarded by the Courts/Tribunals should be just and proper compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case.
It should neither be a meager amount of compensation, nor a Bonanza.
8. Now this Court shall examine as to whether the compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper compensation in the given facts and circumstances of the case.
9. In the case in hand, the Tribunal has awarded Rs. 25,000/- towards physical injury suffered by the applicant.

As per Dr. P.C. Deshmukh (PW-1), disability certificate Exhibit P-1 of the applicant was issued by him to the extent of 12% disability and as per the statement of Dr. Arun Madaria (PW-3), surgery of left arm of the applicant was performed, extending to the shoulder, and a rod was also inserted.
In view of above, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Tribunal ought to have assessed Rs.50,000/- towards physical injury suffered by the applicant instead of Rs.25,000/-.
Ordered accordingly.

10. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- towards physical and mental agony, Rs. 50,000/-
towards medical expenses, Rs. 5,000/- towards transportation expenses, Rs.5,000/- towards attendant, Rs.5,000/- towards nutritious diet and Rs.5,000/-
towards other expenses which are just and proper and required no interference. However, the applicant is entitled for loss of income during treatment and for future treatment.

Hence,
Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment and Rs.10,000/- towards future treatment, according to the above discussion, the compensation amount under various heads in favor of the injured appellant is calculated as under:-
S.No. Heads Calculation  01 Towards physical injury suffered Rs. 50,000/-
 by the applicant  02 Towards physical and mental Rs. 25,000/-
 agony  03 Towards medical expenses Rs. 50,000/-
 04 Towards transportation expenses Rs.5,000/-
05 Towards attendant Rs.5,000/-

06 Towards nutritious diet Rs.5,000/-
 07

Towards other expenses Rs.5,000/-
 08

Towards loss of income during Rs.10,000/-
 treatment  09
Towards future treatment Rs.10,000/-

3 11.
Thus, the total compensation is recomputed as Rs. 1,65,000/-.

After deducting Rs. 1,20,000/- as awarded by the tribunal, the enhancement would be Rs. 45,000/-.
12.
In the result, the appeal is partly allowed.

The appellant/claimant shall be entitled to Rs.
45,000/- in addition to what is already awarded by the claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of enhancement of the award till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the above extent and rest of the conditions shall remain intact.

13. The Registry is further directed to communicate the claimants in writing "the enhanced amount"
in this appeal as against the award made by the Tribunal below.

The said communication be made in Hindi Deonagri language and the help of paralegal workers may be availed with a co-ordination of Secretary, Legal Aid of the concerned area wherein the claimants resides.

Sd/-
